title: Macroeconomic Sentiment and Inflation Database — Data Dictionary
description: Structural and descriptive metadata for all database objects (tables, views) and file-based datasets used in the project. Each entry documents column names, SQL/file data types, constraints, business meaning, and example values.
author: Zahra Younes Pour Langaroudi

schemas.description: Core schema holding normalized, cleaned data loaded from the ETL pipeline. Tables in this schema are the single source of truth for all downstream analytics.
Analytics schema containing derived views that aggregate and join core tables for ML feature extraction and exploratory analysis.

tables.name: core_daily_news
tables.description: Stores one row per financial news article with its FinBERT-derived sentiment score and label. Granularity: one article per row. Populated from the processed FinBERT output file via the ETL notebook.
tables.recordGranularity: One row per news article per day

columns.name: article_id
columns.description: Auto-incrementing surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each news article.

columns.name: news_date
columns.description: Publication date of the news article, normalized to YYYY-MM-DD format.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Headline or title text of the news article. Used as the input to the FinBERT sentiment model.
columns.example: Blackstone boosts IPO after Beijing takes $3bn stake

columns.name: source_name
columns.description: Name of the originating news source (e.g., 'kaggle', 'HuggingFace').

columns.name: source_region
columns.description: Geographic region tag assigned to the article. Used for joining sentiment with the corresponding macroeconomic agency. Values: 'US' or 'Global'.

columns.name: sentiment_score
columns.description: FinBERT-derived sentiment score for the article title. Range: -1.0 (most negative) to +1.0 (most positive). Computed as: P(positive) - P(negative) from the FinBERT softmax output.

columns.name: sentiment_label
columns.description: Categorical sentiment classification derived from the highest-probability FinBERT class.

columns.name: lake_pointer_url
columns.description: URL or file path pointing back to the original raw data source in the data lake. Provides traceability from the database record to its raw origin.

tables.name: core_macro_indicators_monthly
tables.description: Stores monthly macroeconomic indicator values sourced from FRED (US) and Eurostat (EU). Each row represents one month's readings from one source agency. A composite alternate key on (month_date, source_agency) prevents duplicate entries.
tables.recordGranularity: One row per source agency per calendar month

columns.name: record_id
columns.description: Auto-incrementing surrogate primary key.

columns.name: month_date
columns.description: First day of the calendar month this record represents (e.g., 2007-01-01 for January 2007).

columns.name: source_agency
columns.description: The data provider agency. Used in join logic with news sentiment region mapping.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country or economic area the indicators belong to.

columns.name: cpi_value
columns.description: Consumer Price Index value for the given month. For FRED this is the CPIAUCSL series (All Urban Consumers, seasonally adjusted). For Eurostat this is the HICP (prc_hicp_midx).

columns.name: unemployment_rate
columns.description: Monthly unemployment rate as a percentage. FRED series: UNRATE.

columns.name: fed_funds_rate
columns.description: Effective Federal Funds Rate (monthly average). FRED series: FEDFUNDS. NULL for non-US agencies.

columns.name: ind_production_value
columns.description: Industrial Production Index value. FRED series: INDPRO (seasonally adjusted, 2017=100 base).

tables.name: Analytics_Monthly_View
tables.description: Aggregated analytical view joining monthly sentiment averages with macroeconomic indicators. Includes Month-over-Month (MoM) derived calculations for CPI and Industrial Production using SQL window functions (LAG). Designed for ML feature extraction and time-series analysis.
tables.recordGranularity: One row per source agency per calendar month
tables.joinLogic: Sentiment source_region is mapped to indicator source_agency: US→FRED, Global→Eurostat

columns.name: month_date
columns.description: First day of the analysis month, derived from snapping news_date to the 1st of each month.

columns.name: source_agency
columns.description: The macroeconomic data provider (FRED or Eurostat).

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country or economic area.

columns.name: avg_monthly_sentiment
columns.description: Average FinBERT sentiment score across all articles published in the given month and region. Computed via AVG() aggregation on daily article scores.

columns.name: cpi_value
columns.description: Consumer Price Index for the month.

columns.name: unemployment_rate
columns.description: Monthly unemployment rate.

columns.name: fed_funds_rate
columns.description: Federal Funds Rate for the month.

columns.name: ind_production_value
columns.description: Industrial Production Index for the month.

columns.name: cpi_mom
columns.description: Month-over-Month change in CPI, calculated as current month CPI minus the previous month's CPI using the LAG() window function, partitioned by source_agency.
columns.source: Derived via LAG(cpi_value, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY source_agency ORDER BY month_date)

columns.name: ind_production_mom
columns.description: Month-over-Month change in Industrial Production Index, calculated as current minus previous month using the LAG() window function, partitioned by source_agency.
columns.source: Derived via LAG(ind_production_value, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY source_agency ORDER BY month_date)

fileDatasets.name: FinSen_US_Categorized_Timestamp.csv
fileDatasets.description: Raw financial news dataset from the Kaggle FinSen collection. Contains US-focused financial headlines with timestamps and topic tags. This file is treated as immutable after initial download.

columns.name: article_id
columns.description: Unique identifier for each article, assigned during data preparation.

columns.name: Title
columns.description: Headline or title of the financial news article.

columns.name: Tag
columns.description: Topic category tag (e.g., 'News', 'Balance of Trade', 'GDP', 'Inflation Rate').

columns.name: Time
columns.description: Publication date in day/month/year format. Parsed and normalized to DATE during ETL.

columns.name: Content
columns.description: Full article text content including the headline, country tag, topic, body text, and ISO timestamp.

fileDatasets.name: finbert_article_scores.csv
fileDatasets.description: Pre-computed FinBERT sentiment scores for each news article. Generated by running the FinBERT transformer model on article titles. This file serves as a checkpoint to avoid re-running expensive GPU inference.

columns.name: article_id
columns.description: Foreign reference to the raw article. Matches the article_id in the raw news file.

columns.name: Date
columns.description: Publication date, normalized to ISO 8601 format.

columns.name: Title
columns.description: Article headline text that was scored by FinBERT.

columns.name: Sentiment_Score
columns.description: FinBERT sentiment score. Range: -1.0 to +1.0. Calculated as P(positive) - P(negative).

columns.name: Label
columns.description: Categorical sentiment label: 'positive', 'negative', or 'neutral'.
